subject: Clarifying exportable audit/access-log slices, residency copies & deletion proof
messages:
From: Jocelyn Park <jocelyn@acmehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: export & deletion details for audit/access logs (ACME)

Hi Sofia —

We're preparing our SOC2 evidence package and need to confirm how Redwood handles audit and access logs for our tenant. Specifically: 

- What are the default retention periods for (a) admin/audit logs (who changed what) and (b) request/access logs (API requests, IPs, timestamps)?
- Can we request a scoped export (by user ID(s) and time range) that includes full metadata and original IPs? What formats are supported (CSV/NDJSON/etc.)?
- If we terminate or request deletion, what is the deletion timeline for logs and are there resident copies in other regions that must also be deleted?
- What evidence (manifest, checksum, signed attestation) do you provide that proves deletion completed?

We need enough detail to add to our compliance binder; if you have a short export example and expected SLAs that would be great.

Thanks,
Jocelyn
Sr. InfoSec Manager, ACME Health

[Attachment: acme_evidence_req_202709.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jocelyn Park <jocelyn@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: export & deletion details for audit/access logs (ACME)

Hi Jocelyn —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and an attached export plan for reference. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you'd prefer a walkthrough.

Summary (defaults / options):
- Admin/audit logs (console/admin actions): default retention 365 days for hosted tenants; configurable up to 7 years on enterprise plans.
- Request/access logs (API requests, worker traces, source IPs): default retention 90 days; customers on Dedicated/Private can request longer retention or local-only retention to satisfy residency needs.
- Scoped exports: supported. You can filter by tenant_id, user_id(s), resource_id(s), and arbitrary time range. Export formats: NDJSON (recommended), gzip'd CSV, and compressed Parquet for large windows.
- Export delivery: direct S3 push to a customer S3 bucket (preferred), or time-limited presigned HTTPS bundle. Exports include a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums) and a machine-readable schema.
- Deletion & residency: when deletion is requested, primary tenant data and logs are removed within 30 days by default. If you request a certified deletion (recommended for regulated customers), we perform a two-stage process: snapshot & hash, push export if requested, then crypto-erase keys and delete copies across regions; final deletion confirmation delivered as a signed deletion manifest.

Details:
- Scoping and fields: exports include timestamp, request_id, method, path, response_code, latency_ms, user_id (if present), actor_email, source_ip (unless masked), service_node, and request_headers (redaction configurable). See attached export_field_map.csv for the full column list.
- Residency behavior: for hosted tenants, we maintain hot logs in the tenant region and a replicated cold copy for resilience. Replication is region-aware: by default we replicate to a nearby region within the same geography (US->US, EU->EU). For strict residency, Dedicated/Private customers can opt out of cross-region replication and keep exports local.
- Deletion holds & legal requests: legal/retention holds will override deletion; we surface any holds in the deletion manifest.

I've attached audit_export_plan.md which outlines the typical export flow and provides examples. Next steps: if you can confirm the exact fields you need and whether ACME wants raw IPs or masked IPs, we'll prepare an export estimate and an SLA for delivery.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Compliance & Security Partner, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: audit_export_plan.md (markdown, 28KB)]

From: Jocelyn Park <jocelyn@acmehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Compliance <compliance@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: export & deletion details for audit/access logs (ACME)

Thanks Sofia — a couple quick clarifying items before we proceed: 

1) Scoped export: if we request a 3-month window for ~120k events filtered to three service accounts, is the NDJSON export functionally identical to what is stored in your hot/store? Are IPs included verbatim?
2) Replication: you mentioned "cold copy" in another region — is that retained for the same retention period or is it a rolling backup with a shorter TTL?
3) Deletion proof: we need a signed artifact that shows which files were deleted, the checksums, and the timestamp (UTC). Can you provide a sample of that manifest?

Also, do you offer an expedited export option (24-48 hours) for compliance incidents and what the surcharge looks like?

Appreciate it,
Jocelyn

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jocelyn Park <jocelyn@acmehealth.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: export & deletion details for audit/access logs (ACME)

Hi Jocelyn —

I'll take the operational details on the items you flagged. Long answer but wanted to be explicit.

1) NDJSON fidelity & IPs: yes — the NDJSON export is a full event dump and mirrors the on-platform shape. For hosted tenants we include source_ip by default. For customers who require pseudonymization we offer an export option that buckets IPs to /24 or replaces with a persistent hash. 

2) Replication TTL: cold replicas are a rolling store with slightly longer TTL defaults to support restores. Default retention policies: hot store = configured retention (90d access, 365d audit), cold replica = configured retention + 30 days buffer. If you choose "no cross-region replication" for residency, replicas are not copied outside the selected geography.

3) Signed deletion manifest: we produce a manifest that lists every object removed, the preceding SHA256, UTC deletion timestamp, and the operator id. For certified deletions we also include a PGP-signed statement from our compliance team. Sample attached: signed_deletion_manifest_template.pdf.

4) SLAs & expedited exports: standard export SLA for < 1M events is 3 business days. For windows under 30 days and < 200k events, turnaround is typically 48–72 hours. Expedited 24-hour delivery is available for incidents and is an add-on (billing code HBSP-48291).

Operational notes:
- Export delivery: we'll put the files in your S3 bucket with server-side encryption; we also provide the signed manifest and a delivery verification step (manifest + checksum compared to uploaded objects).
- Deletion timeline: after export and customer confirmation, we delete the tenant's logs from the hot store immediately and from the cold replica within 30 days; final manifest delivered on completion.

Let me know if you want a quick runbook (I can send one) or a call to walk through the S3 permissions required.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Platform Ops, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: export_field_map.csv (csv, 12KB)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jocelyn Park <jocelyn@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T16:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: export & deletion details for audit/access logs (ACME)

Adding a couple of implementation-level guarantees and the next steps: 

- Proof-of-deletion workflow: once you confirm export receipt, we generate a signed deletion manifest and a cryptographic proof (SHA256 tree hash over the set of deleted objects). The manifest contains: object name, size, SHA256, deletion timestamp (UTC), operator id, and 'hold' flag if applicable.
- Key management: if you require, we can push the export to a bucket encrypted with your KMS key; deletion will then include crypto-erase steps where applicable (we zero the KMS key material so that server-side copies become unreadable).
- Auditability: every export and deletion action is logged to our internal immutable audit ledger (retained per your contract), and we can provide a time-ordered slice on request for reviewers.

Next steps: 
1) Confirm whether ACME wants raw IPs or masked values in the export.
2) Confirm S3 destination + KMS ARN (if you want us to push).
3) If you need an expedited export, confirm HBSP-48291 and we'll scope the work and cost.

I'll prepare the deletion manifest template for your legal team to review and can schedule a 30-minute handoff with our SREs to finalize the S3 permissions.

—Aditya
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: signed_deletion_manifest_template.pdf (pdf, 8KB)]
